annotations.note: This project lock/restore specification is preserved exactly. The following annotations provide secure guidance to implement authentication, authorization, and CORS in the application code without changing project behavior.

security_recommendations.authentication: Add JWT (or cookie) based authentication in your Program.cs/Startup. Use Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer and Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens. Do not expose secrets in source; keep them in secure configuration (user secrets / environment variables / Key Vault).
security_recommendations.authorization: Define role-based authorization policies and apply [Authorize] and policy-based attributes on controllers or endpoints. Example roles: 'Admin', 'User'. Always validate tokens and enforce least privilege.
security_recommendations.cors: Restrict CORS in production to explicit origins. Maintain a separate development configuration that can use relaxed policies (for example: AllowLocalDevelopment). Never use AllowAnyOrigin in production. Store allowed origins in configuration (appsettings.Production.json or secure environment variables).

implementation_guidance: Do not change dependencies in this auto-generated restore file directly to enable authentication; instead add NuGet package references in your .csproj (e.g., Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer) and update source code as shown in the snippet.
Use environment-specific appsettings (appsettings.Development.json, appsettings.Production.json) and environment variables for sensitive configuration like Jwt:Key and CORS origins.
Apply [Authorize] and role policies on controllers. Example: [Authorize(Roles="Admin")] or [Authorize(Policy="RequireAdminRole")].
